CHROMIUM: platform/chrome: wilco_ec: Add charge scheduling backend This patch adds the backend to support to control two charge-scheduling policies managed by the EC, Advanced Charging and Peak Shift. Advanced Charging Mode maximizes the battery health by adjusting the charging algorithm throughout the day. When enabled, the system will use standard charging algorithms and other techniques during non-work hours to maximize battery health. During work hours, an express charge is used, allowing the battery to be charged faster. For each day the time in which the system will be most heavily used is specified by the start time and the duration. Peak Shift is power saving policy that minimizes AC usage during the peak usage times of the day. For each weekday a start, end, and charge_start time to run in Peak Shift mode can be set. After the start time the system will run from the battery even if the AC is attached, as long as the battery stays above a specified threshold. After the end time the system will run from AC (if attached) but will not charge the battery. The system will again function normally (use AC and recharge the battery) after the charge_start time. BUG=b:128524060, b:125011171 TEST=With following patches this library works. Change-Id: I39cde67294a315add09576fe870bc456b70bd43c Signed-off-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1590689 Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: platform/chrome: wilco_ec: Add charge scheduling sysfs This patch adds support to control two charge scheduling policies managed by the EC, Peak Shift and Advanced Charging. Peak Shift is a power saving policy that minimizes AC usage during the peak usage times of the day. Advanced Charging Mode maximizes the battery health by adjusting the charging algorithm throughout the day. For userspace interface and more info see Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-platform-wilco-ec I am applying this locally to Chromium because I want to get this in by M75, and it currently is not acceptable by upstream. There is a publicly viewable Google Doc [1] that I have been working on with Enric Balletbo i Serra (the platform/chrome maintainer) and Sebastian Reichel (the power system maintainer) to figure out a generalized API to control charge scheduling for Linux. I have structured this code in such a way that the sysfs interface and the EC communication backend are separate, so that in the future, if the user-facing interface changes, the backend can be re-used. [1] https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ipuxwWUm1G6WRt_tDqNxBniaE49AJ7JnF0BSaNek9Gc BUG=b:128524060, b:125011171 TEST=On the device, try: localhost # cd /sys/bus/platform/devices/GOOG000C:00/wilco-charge-schedule localhost # cat advanced_charging_tuesday 09:30 08:15 localhost # echo 7:30 13:45 18:00 > peak_shift_sunday localhost # cat peak_shift_battery_threshold 88 Change-Id: I148d3ff29b1d37532fcfa4fd22da91f9b1b5f5ae Signed-off-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1586182 Reviewed-by: Daniel Kurtz <djkurtz@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Simon Glass <sjg@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: adapter: Prevent caching discoverable and its timeout in persist file Currently setting discoverable to a certain value is written in the persist file which will be used for resuming the discvoerable state after reboot. In the case where an application can set discoverable to true and fail to set it back to false intentionally or unintentionally later, the device can stuck discoverable forever even after reboot. Therefore, this patch makes discoverable setting to be volatile by not reading from the persist file and not storing the new setting into the persist file. BUG=chromium:942683 TEST=(1)run bluetoothctl set discoverable to true and verify that discoverable setting was not written to the persist file (2)set discoverable to true and discoverable timeout to 0 in /var/lib/bluetooth/{adapter}/settings, restart bluetoothd and verify discoverable state is not set to true Change-Id: I753c99460af270897e05c8f5b7c1d06b24d7df47 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1584786 Commit-Ready: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Tested-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ryan Hansberry <hansberry@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org>

nvmem: protect flash accesses with a mutex Multiple tasks could be trying to modify NVMEM concurrently. To avoid data corruption add a mutex which guarantees that only one thread of execution has access to the flash storing NVMEM objects. Various paths accessing flash contents are now protected by the same mutex. Mutex control functions are put in wrappers, which makes it easier to add debugging code when needed. biod: Add retries for device init operations This CL adds an additional retry to the critical fingerprint MCU probing operations, which take place during biod startup. The error can be reproduced using the stress tester in CL:1556384 (patchset 11). The same stress tester was used to verify that this solution. Reads and ioctls to the fingerprint MCU (/dev/cros_fp) have been shown to occasionally fail with ETIMEDOUT. If a read/cmd fails during the startup of biod, it may be led to believe that the system does not have a fingerprint sensor/mcu. This renders the fingerprint system inoperable until a reboot is issued. Failures during the runtime of biod are less critical, since the operation can be reattempted by the user. This patchset does not cover the entire startup process. A followup patchset will enable retries for the remaining startup operations. BUG=b:128011695 TEST=stress test to ensure 2 attempts is sufficient CL:1556384 TEST=implementation verified with stress tester in CL:1556384 PS 21 TEST=unit tests, emerged, deployed to nocturne TEST=enrolled and used fingerprint Change-Id: Ie0b849f9884f81fe75900ffd4b2652d1e1ef2e9d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1559501 Commit-Ready: Craig Hesling <hesling@chromium.org> Tested-by: Craig Hesling <hesling@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Norvez <norvez@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Fix MGMT opcodes conflict in BlueZ kernel 4.19 defines two new MGMT opcodes for new LE PHY rates. These conflict with existing opcodes in MGMT. The new BlueZ opcodes are not being used by BlueZ user space, so this fix just allocated new opcodes for them. Since these are LE PHY updates, in the long term they will be part of NewBlue, so they are not planned to be used by BlueZ user space at all.
